findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the sweep-start recovery preamble discriminates an abandoned partial fold (revert) from the intentionally-retained SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state that `_retire_folded_sources` keeps for `fsck --repair-snapshots` (never revert), e.g. via an in-progress fold marker or a commit-pending sentinel.
evidence: Plan: 'a sweep-start crash-recovery preamble that reverts an abandoned partial fold under the write lock'

compact_txn.py:300-322 documents a deliberate retained state: 'We MUST intentionally RETAIN the SNAPSHOT here ... Retaining it leaves a SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state ... that fsck --repair-snapshots already rebuilds. Do NOT simplify this back into an unconditional os.remove(final_path).'

A partial-fold on-disk (SNAPSHOT written, some sources .retired, no commit) is byte-for-byte similar to the intentionally-retained incomplete-rollback state; without a discriminator the preamble may revert state the existing code chose to keep.
findings.finding: The crash-recovery preamble for the compaction fold does not specify how it distinguishes an ABANDONED partial fold (worker died mid-fold) from the INTENTIONAL SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state that `_retire_folded_sources` deliberately retains on incomplete rollback.
findings.location: Child decomposition: 'Crash-atomic compaction fold' + AC line 1
scenarios: Worker dies after atomic_write of SNAPSHOT but before commit — preamble must revert
Prior fold hit an incomplete-rollback (reverse-rename failed) and deliberately kept the SNAPSHOT for fsck — preamble must NOT revert

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion covering push-recovery parity (bug sulfuryl-suicidal-osprey): non-fast-forward push recovers both untracked-collision and tracked-deletion aborts, with a RED->GREEN test proxy.
evidence: Child bullet: 'Push-recovery parity (bug sulfuryl-suicidal-osprey): the non-fast-forward push recovery path gets the same untracked-collision + tracked-deletion recovery as reconverge.'
AC list covers compaction (AC1), reconverge _union_merge (AC2), markers (AC3), fsck/doctor (AC4), scan scoping (AC5), mitigation removal (AC6) — no AC references push recovery.
findings.finding: The 'Push-recovery parity' child (bug sulfuryl-suicidal-osprey) — giving the non-fast-forward push recovery path the same untracked-collision + tracked-deletion recovery — has no covering acceptance criterion.
scenarios: A non-fast-forward push after a wedge is left unrecovered while reconverge is fixed, silently missing the parity deliverable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add e72e acceptance criteria for the crash-atomic fold (commit-as-one-unit + rollback) AND the sweep-start recovery preamble, with a kill-mid-fold test asserting git status --porcelain empty after the next sweep, satisfying parent AC1's sweep half.
evidence: Parent AC1: 'A compaction fold interrupted at any point between its first worktree mutation and its commit leaves the tracker tree clean after the next sweep or doctor run; proxy: kill-mid-fold unit test asserts git status --porcelain is empty post-recovery.'
e72e (the crash-atomic fold child that owns the sweep-start recovery preamble per the parent decomposition) has no '## Acceptance Criteria' block in the material under review.
c925's ACs cover 'doctor --repair heals a seeded wedge' (the doctor half) but not the kill-mid-fold sweep-start recovery proxy.
findings.finding: Parent AC1's sweep-side proxy ('leaves the tracker tree clean after the next sweep ... proxy: kill-mid-fold unit test asserts git status --porcelain is empty post-recovery') is owned by e72e, whose roster block is title-only with no parseable acceptance criteria. The 'or doctor run' clause is covered by c925, but the kill-mid-fold sweep-recovery half is delivered by no sibling with parseable AC — indeterminate.
scenarios: The crash-atomic fold + sweep-start recovery preamble ships without a kill-mid-fold unit test asserting a clean git status post-recovery; a partial fold from a killed detached worker is left dirty until a doctor run, contradicting the 'after the next sweep' guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit ACs to e72e for (1) atomic fold with rollback and (2) sweep-start crash-recovery preamble, each with a kill-mid-fold RED->GREEN test asserting clean status post-sweep.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Populate 573a with scope + acceptance criteria mirroring a560's recovery (untracked-collision + tracked-deletion, quarantine-never-delete, single retry) and declare its dependency on a560's shared recovery seam.
evidence: 573a child block under review has an empty body (title only); show_ticket confirms description is empty.
Parent decomposition: 'Push-recovery parity (bug sulfuryl-suicidal-osprey): the non-fast-forward push recovery path gets the same untracked-collision + tracked-deletion recovery as reconverge.'
Parent Acceptance Criteria list contains no push-recovery item — so no parent AC is uncovered by 573a's silence.
573a title says it 'resets tracked-only, leaves colliding untracked leftovers' — the same recovery shape a560 builds; reuse implies dependency on a560.
findings.finding: Push-recovery parity child 573a is presented title-only (empty description, no scope or acceptance criteria). The parent decomposition says it 'gets the same untracked-collision + tracked-deletion recovery as reconverge' (a560's seam), implying a build-order/reuse dependency on a560, but no dependency or AC is stated. Coverage/consistency of 573a is indeterminate; the parent AC set has no push-recovery criterion, so this is a consistency (dependency-gap) observation rather than a parent-AC coverage gap.
scenarios: 573a is scheduled/built before a560 defines the shared tracked-deletion+untracked-collision recovery seam, forcing 573a to invent the recovery independently or duplicate it, creating scope overlap and divergent implementations of the same recovery across push_recovery.py and sync.py.
findings.suggested_fix: Add ACs to 573a for both recovery classes on the push non-fast-forward path and a dep on a560 so the shared recovery logic is reused rather than reimplemented.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit acceptance criterion to e72e (crash-atomic fold child) requiring removal of the user-config compact.trigger=off block AND a closing comment on e72e recording the removal, satisfying parent AC6.
evidence: Parent AC: 'The interim user-config compact.trigger=off mitigation is removed once the crash-atomicity child closes; proxy: closing comment on e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73 records the removal.'

e72e roster/child block presents only the '### child' title and description (PROPOSED ROOT CAUSE / PROPOSED FIX) with NO '## Acceptance Criteria' list — its description note 'REMOVE the user-config block when closing this ticket' is prose, not a listed AC.
Per the absence rule, a sibling showing only its title has no parseable criteria and is indeterminate for coverage.
findings.finding: Parent AC6 ('the interim user-config compact.trigger=off mitigation is removed once the crash-atomicity child closes; proxy: closing comment on e72e records the removal') is assigned to e72e, whose roster block shows only its title line with no parseable acceptance criteria. No other sibling's roster AC delivers this observable outcome (removing the user-config block / closing comment). Coverage is therefore indeterminate rather than confirmed.
scenarios: e72e closes as done but the completion verifier finds no AC guaranteeing the compact.trigger=off block was removed and no closing comment recorded on e72e; the interim mitigation silently persists in ~/.config/rebar/config.toml, leaving operation-linked sweeps disabled after the durable fix landed.
findings.suggested_fix: Give e72e a parseable AC mirroring parent AC6 (remove the user-config compact.trigger=off block; record removal in a closing comment on e72e), so AC6 is covered by a named child AC rather than a description note.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the path-selective restore/quarantine for variant-b over reusing push_recovery's existing generic stash-commit dirty-tree dance, OR reuse that proven mechanism in reconverge so both paths converge on one recovery strategy.
evidence: Plan reconverge child: 'restore worktree-deleted tracked files from HEAD, quarantine modified ones, retry once'
Plan push child: 'gets the same untracked-collision + tracked-deletion recovery as reconverge'

push_recovery.py:272 `if _DIRTY_WD.search(...)` routes to `_recover_dirty_merge` (lines 120-180) which handles a dirty tree GENERICALLY: `_stash_create` -> `reset --hard` -> merge -> `_restore_stash` — no per-path classification needed
Asking push to match reconverge inverts the existing direction: the more robust generic stash-dance already lives in push and would be a candidate to reuse in reconverge instead.
findings.finding: The plan proposes a bespoke path-selective tracked-artifact recovery for reconverge (restore worktree-deleted tracked files from HEAD, quarantine modified ones) and then asks push to adopt 'the same' recovery, but push already recovers a dirty tree generically via a stash-commit dance; the plan neither reuses that proven mechanism nor states why a new path-selective approach is preferable.
findings.location: Child decomposition: 'Reconverge tracked-artifact recovery' and 'Push-recovery parity'
scenarios: A reconverge faces variant-b (local tracked-file deletions/mods) — a stash-dance would recover ANY dirty tracked state, whereas restore-from-HEAD+quarantine only covers the enumerated store-artifact classes
Push-recovery parity work may end up REPLACING a working generic mechanism with a narrower one

T5e: a novel architectural decision must be captured in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify old+new coexistence during rollout: how the store stays wedge-proof while some sessions still run pre-atomic compaction code, and the ordering for re-enabling compact.trigger across concurrently-running sessions.
evidence: Context: 'chronically wedged under parallel multi-session writes' and 'Interim mitigation active: user-config compact.trigger=off'.
AC6 removes the mitigation but does not state how old sessions (still running non-atomic compaction) coexist with new sessions during the transition.
T12: if coordinated services change, deploy order and old+new coexistence must be specified.
findings.finding: The store is explicitly shared across parallel multi-session writes, yet the plan does not address old+new coexistence during rollout: while the change lands, some sessions still run the pre-atomic compaction code and can produce the exact dirty tree the new recovery expects to prevent. Re-enabling compaction (removing compact.trigger=off, AC6) across a fleet of concurrently-running sessions has no stated deploy ordering or coexistence guarantee.
findings.location: Context (interim mitigation) + AC6 'compact.trigger=off mitigation is removed once the crash-atomicity child closes'
findings.suggested_fix: Note that the self-healing sync/push recovery and doctor repair must land (and the recovery paths tolerate dirty trees produced by any still-running old-code session) BEFORE compact.trigger is re-enabled, so recovery covers the coexistence window.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a concurrency-safe execution mechanism for the marker-untrack migration on the shared branch (e.g. detached temp index + write-tree/commit-tree + CAS update-ref as in _purge_committed_reconciler_locks, or run under the exclusive write lock), and state how writes landing DURING the migration are preserved.
evidence: Plan: 'Untrack per-ticket runtime markers (*/.archived, */.write.lock) from the tickets branch via an idempotent ensure unit'

RCA comment on 6ccc-0577-198c-44fa: '~90 .tickets-tracker dirs are separate worktrees sharing one .git ... one HEAD ... one object store'; 'The shared tracker is being actively written by other sessions right now (HEAD advanced 7ec1742 -> b7b1c7b during this investigation)'

Existing codebase precedent for this exact migration class: rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:310-356 _purge_committed_reconciler_locks prunes committed branch files via a DETACHED temp index + write-tree/commit-tree + CAS update-ref so 'the main worktree/index is never touched, and the CAS makes a concurrent writer safe'
ABSENCE: plan text names no detached-index/CAS mechanism, no write-lock scoping, and no dual-write-window handling for the untrack commit
findings.finding: The marker-untracking migration (git-tree change removing ~245 tracked */.archived + */.write.lock entries from HEAD) does not specify a concurrency-safe execution mechanism for a store that is actively written by ~90 worktrees sharing one object store, so writes committed DURING the migration can collide or be lost.
findings.location: Child decomposition: 'Untrack per-ticket runtime markers ... via an idempotent ensure unit'; AC line 'git ls-files ... returns empty after the ensure unit runs'
scenarios: The ensure unit runs git rm --cached against the shared main worktree/index while a peer session commits a ticket event concurrently, corrupting the index or dropping the peer commit
Two worktrees each run the ensure unit simultaneously and race on the branch tip
findings.suggested_fix: Have the ensure unit prune */.archived and */.write.lock in a detached index and CAS-advance refs/heads/tickets (mirroring rebar_reconciler._purge_committed_reconciler_locks), retrying on CAS contention, so the main worktree/index is untouched and concurrent writers are never lost; add an AC asserting no concurrent write is dropped during the migration.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the back-out path for the marker-untrack migration and add an AC asserting the post-rollback store state stays wedge-safe (or, if reverting re-arms the wedge, document that reverting is unsupported and default to compensating-forward via the ensure unit / doctor).
evidence: Plan AC only asserts state AFTER the ensure unit runs ('returns empty', 'churn no longer appears in git status') — never after a back-out of the migration commit

RCA comment: the tracked-dirt class exists precisely because markers were 'committed to HEAD before the gitignore pattern was added' and 'gitignore never un-tracks already-tracked files' — so re-tracking (via revert) re-arms the wedge
ABSENCE: plan names no back-out path for the untrack commit and no assertion that reverting it leaves the store in a safe (non-wedged) interpretation
findings.finding: The untrack migration narrows what the tickets branch tracks (a track/read-path narrowing), but no back-out path is defined and no acceptance criterion asserts the post-rollback state — if the untrack commit is reverted, the markers become tracked in HEAD again and the tracked-dirt wedge class silently returns.
findings.location: AC line 'git ls-files '*/.archived' '*/.write.lock' ... returns empty after the ensure unit runs'; Child 'Untrack per-ticket runtime markers'
scenarios: An operator reverts the untrack commit to undo a suspected regression; markers re-enter HEAD, marker churn re-appears as tracked dirt, and plan-review/close attestations begin failing the strict git status --porcelain check again
findings.suggested_fix: State that the untrack is compensating-forward only: reverting the commit is unsupported because it re-tracks the markers and re-arms the wedge; the sanctioned back-out is to re-run the idempotent ensure unit (or rebar doctor --repair). Add an AC that verifies re-running the ensure unit after any manual re-track restores git ls-files to empty.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Declare c925's dependency on a560 (variant-(b) reconverge recovery) landing first, OR scope c925's doctor repair to fully clean the tree so its post-repair reconverge cannot hit an unrecovered variant-(b) abort.
evidence: c925 Approach: 'After healing, invoke the existing reconverge entry (rebar._store.sync.reconverge) so a previously wedged store converges in the same command.'
c925 AC: 'rebar doctor --repair heals a seeded wedge end-to-end (... merge converged ...)'.
a560 owns variant-(b) reconverge recovery; parent decomposition orders untrack-markers first but does not state c925 depends on a560.

c925's own repair restores class-1 and quarantines class-2 before reconverge, which may leave the store in a state where reconverge only needs to re-merge — but the AC's 'merge converged' with a diverged origin relies on reconverge handling any residual variant-(b) abort.
findings.finding: Dependency gap: c925 (fsck/doctor) plans to 'invoke the existing reconverge entry (rebar._store.sync.reconverge) so a previously wedged store converges in the same command' as part of doctor --repair, but a560 is the child that teaches reconverge to recover abort variant (b). Neither c925 nor the parent decomposition declares c925's dependency on a560 landing first. If doctor --repair runs before a560 lands, its post-repair reconverge can hit the unhandled variant-(b) abort and fail to converge — yet c925's own AC asserts 'the store converges'.
scenarios: c925 is implemented/tested before a560 merges; the seeded-wedge end-to-end test spins up a diverged origin, doctor repairs local dirt then calls reconverge, which aborts on a residual tracked-file variant-(b) condition it cannot yet recover, and c925's 'merge converged' AC fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit dep 'c925 depends on a560' (or state in c925's plan that repair fully neutralizes variant-(b) conditions before the reconverge call), so the 'merge converged' AC holds regardless of build order.
